p.docTitle:
Ordinance
on Protection against Dangerous Substances and Preparations

preamble.p:
based on Article 19 paragraphs 2 and 3 of the Animal Welfare Act of
16 December 2005
SR 455 ,
on the Chemicals Act of 15 December 2000
SR 813.1 (ChemA),
on Article 26 paragraph 3, 29, 30a–30d, 38 paragraph 3, 39 paragraph 1, 41 paragraph 3, 44 paragraphs 2 and 3, 46 paragraphs 2 and 3 and 48 paragraph 2 of the Federal Act of 7 October 1983
SR 814.01 on the Protection of the Environment (EPA),
and on Article 9 paragraph 2 letter c, 27 paragraph 2 and 48 paragraph 2 of the Waters Protection Act of 24 January 1991
SR 814.20 ,
and in implementation of the Federal Act of 6 October 1995
SR 946.51 on Technical Barriers to Trade,
Amended by No I of the O of 31 Jan. 2018, in force since 1 March 2018 (AS 2018 801).

blockList.listIntroduction: This Ordinance regulates:

item.p: the determination and assessment of dangers and risks that substances and preparations may pose to human life and health and to the environment;
the conditions under which substances and preparations that may endanger people or the environment are placed on the market;
the handling of substances and preparations that may endanger people or the environment;
the way in which data relating to substances and preparations is processed by the enforcement authorities.

content.p:
This Ordinance applies to biocidal products and the active substances contained therein, and to plant protection products and the active substances and co-formulants contained therein, insofar as they are referred to in the Ordinance of 18 May 2005 on Biocidal Products
SR 813.12 or the Ordinance of 20 August 2025
SR 916.161 on Plant Protection Products.
Amended by Annex 10 No II 2 of the Plant Protection Products Ordinance of 20 Aug. 2025, in force since 1 Dec. 2025 (AS 2025 565).

This Ordinance applies to tobacco products and electronic cigarettes in terms of Article 3 letters a–f of the Tobacco Products Act of 1 October 2021
SR 818.32 and for similar products that are deemed equivalent thereto in accordance with Article 3 of the Tobacco Products Ordinance of 28 August 2024
SR 818.321 (TabPO) insofar as they are referred to in the TabPO.
Inserted by Annex 4 No II 5 of the Tobacco Products Ordinance of 28 Aug. 2024, in force since 1 Oct. 2024 (AS 2024 491).
This Ordinance applies to radioactive substances and preparations, excluding effects attributable to the radioactive nature of these substances and preparations.

Only Articles 5–7 and 81 apply to cosmetic products within the meaning of Article 53 paragraph 1 of the Ordinance of 16 December 2016
SR 817.02 on Foodstuffs and Utility Articles in the form of finished products intended for private or professional users, and only with regard to environmental protection and to classification or assessment in relation to risks to the environment.
Amended by No I of the O of 31 Jan. 2018, in force since 1 March 2018 (AS 2018 801).

blockList.listIntroduction: This Ordinance does not apply to:

item.p: the transport of substances and preparations by road, rail, water, air or pipelines, with the exception of Article 10 paragraph 1 letter b;
the transit of substances and preparations under customs supervision, provided that this does not involve any processing or transformation;

blockList.listIntroduction:
substances and preparations in the form of finished products ready for supply to private and professional users that fall into the following categories:
Amended by No I of the O of 31 Jan. 2018, in force since 1 March 2018 (AS 2018 801).

item.num:
1.
Amended by No I of the O of 31 Jan. 2018, in force since 1 March 2018 (AS 2018 801).
item.p:
foodstuffs as defined by Article 4 of the Foodstuffs Act of 20 June 2014
SR 817.0 (FoodA),

medicinal products as defined by Article 4 paragraph 1 letter a and medical devices as defined by Article 4 paragraph 1 letter b of the Therapeutic Products Act of 15 December 2000
SR 812.21 ,
substances, preparations and objects which are waste according to Article 7 paragraph 6 of the EPA.

content.p:
Articles 57, 62 and 67 apply to imported substances and preparations that are simply relabelled and then exported without alteration.
Amended by No III 1 of the O of 22 March 2017, in force since 1 May 2017 (AS 2017 2593).

Dangerous substances and preparations that are exported are also governed by the PIC Ordinance of 10 November 2004
SR 814.82 .
Inserted by No III 1 of the O of 22 March 2017, in force since 1 May 2017 (AS 2017 2593).

blockList.listIntroduction: By way of clarification of the definitions given in the Chemicals Act, in this Ordinance:

item.p: substance means a chemical element and its compounds in the natural state or obtained by any manufacturing process, including any additive necessary to preserve its stability and any impurity deriving from the process used, but excluding any solvent which may be separated without affecting the stability of the substance or changing its composition;

blockList.listIntroduction: manufacturer means:

item.p: any natural or legal person domiciled in Switzerland or with a registered office or branch in Switzerland, who manufactures, extracts or imports substances, preparations or objects in a professional or commercial capacity, and

item.num:
2.
Amended by No I of the O of 11 March 2022, in force since 1 May 2022 (AS 2022 220).

blockList.listIntroduction: any person who obtains substances, preparations or objects in Switzerland and supplies them on a commercial basis, without altering their composition:

item.p: under his own name, without specifying the name of the original manufacturer,
under his own trade name,
in packaging other than that provided by the original manufacturer,
for a different intended use, or
at a location where the labelling in accordance with Article 10 paragraph 3 letter b has not been applied in the official language by the original manufacturer,

item.num:
3.
Amended by No I of the O of 31 Jan. 2018, in force since 1 March 2018 (AS 2018 801). The correction of 4 Oct. 2024 relates to the French text only (AS 2024 536).
item.p: a person is deemed to be the sole manufacturer if he arranges for the manufacture of a substance, preparation or object in Switzerland by a third party, and if he is domiciled or has a registered office or branch in Switzerland; if he has neither his domicile, a registered office or branch in Switzerland, the third party is the sole manufacturer.

blockList.listIntroduction: In addition, in this Ordinance:
professional user means:

item.p: any natural or legal person who obtains substances, preparations or objects in Switzerland for use in professional activities,

blockList.listIntroduction: also deemed to be a professional user is:

item.p: any natural or legal person who obtains substances, preparations or objects in Switzerland for use in the course of training or for research purposes,
any legal person who obtains substances, preparations or objects in Switzerland for use in charitable activities;
private user means any natural person who obtains or uses substances, preparations or objects for non-professional purposes;
trader means any natural or legal person who obtains substances, preparations or objects in Switzerland and supplies them unchanged on a commercial basis;

exclusive representative means any natural or legal person that is authorised by a manufacturer whose domicile or registered office is located abroad to notify a substance in Switzerland and represents several importers designated by that manufacturer;

object means an article, consisting of one or more substances or preparations, which during production is given a special shape, surface or design which determines its end use function to a greater degree than does its chemical composition;

item.num:
f.
Amended by No I of the O of 11 March 2022, in force since 1 May 2022 (AS 2022 220).

blockList.listIntroduction:
existing substance means the substance that is registered in accordance with Article 5 of Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 (REACH Regulation)
Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 18 December 2006 concerning the Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals (REACH), establishing a European Chemicals Agency, amending Directive 1999/45/EC and repealing Council Regulation (EEC) No 793/93 and Commission Regulation (EC) No 1488/94 as well as Council Directive 76/769/EEC and Commission Directives 91/155/EEC, 93/67/EEC, 93/105/EC and 2000/21/EC, OJ L 396 of 30.12.2006, p. 1; last amended by Regulation (EU) No (EU) 2021/2204, OJ L 446 of 14.12.2021, p. 34. , with the exception of substances that:

item.num:
1.
The correction of 5 May 2022 concerns the French text only (AS 2022 273).
item.p: are placed on the market in larger quantities than those registered in the European Economic Area (EEA), or
are registered solely as intermediates, unless they are monomers;

blockList.listIntroduction: polymer means a substance consisting of molecules characterised by the sequence of one or more types of monomer units and comprising:

item.p: a simple weight majority of molecules containing at least three monomer units which are covalently bound to at least one other monomer unit or other reactant, and

less than a simple weight majority of molecules of the same molecular weight; these molecules must be distributed over a range of molecular weights wherein differences in the molecular weight are primarily attributable to differences in the number of monomer units;

monomer means a substance which is capable of forming covalent bonds with a sequence of additional like or unlike molecules under the conditions of the relevant polymer-forming reaction used for the particular process;
monomer unit means the reacted form of a monomer substance in a polymer;
intermediate means a substance manufactured and used solely for chemical processing during which it is transformed into one or more other substances;
secondary product means any substance formed by chemical or biochemical transformation during the storage, use or disposal of a substance or preparation;
scientific research and development means any scientific experimentation, analysis or chemical research carried out under controlled conditions and involving quantities of less than 1 tonne per year;

product and process-orientated research and development means any scientific development related to product development or the further development of a substance on its own, in preparations or in objects in the course of which pilot plant or production trials are used to define the production process or test the fields of application of the substance;

robust study summary means a detailed summary of the objectives, methods, results and conclusions of a full study report providing sufficient information to make an independent assessment of the study, minimising the need to consult the full study report;

exposure scenario means the set of conditions, including operational conditions and risk management measures, that describe how the substance is manufactured or used during its life-cycle and how the manufacturer controls, or recommends customers to control, exposures of humans and the environment. These exposure scenarios may cover one specific process or use or several processes or uses as appropriate;
hazard class means the nature of the physical, health or environmental hazard;

nanomaterial means a material containing particles in an unbound state or as an aggregate or as an agglomerate, where one or more external dimensions is in the size range 1–100 nm, or a material where the specific surface area by volume is greater than 60 m2/cm3. A material is only considered to be a nanomaterial if it is deliberately produced to utilise the properties arising from the defined external dimensions of the particles it contains, or from the defined surface area by volume of the material. Fullerenes, graphene flakes and single-wall carbon nanotubes with one or more external dimensions below 1 nm are considered to be nanomaterials;

item.num:
r.
Inserted by No I of the O of 11 March 2022, in force since 1 May 2022 (AS 2022 220).
item.p: colorants means substances and preparations that primarily contain colouring agents, colour pigments and effect-producing pigments which are added solely for the purpose of colouring or producing effects.

content.p: Any other terms which are used in various senses in the legislation underlying this Ordinance are used here as defined in the Chemicals Act.

The equivalence of expressions between the REACH Regulation, Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP Regulation)
Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures, amending and repealing Directives 67/548/EEC and 1999/45/EC and amending Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006, OJ L 353 of 31.12.2008, p. 1; last amended by Delegated Regulation (EU) No 2021/1962, OJ L 400 of 12.11.2021, p. 16. and Directive 75/324/EEC
Council Directive 75/324/EEC of 20 May 1975 on the approximation of the laws of the Member States relating to aerosol dispensers, OJ L 147 of 9.6.1975, p. 40; last amended by Directive (EU) 2016/2037, OJ L 314 of 22.11.2016, p. 11. , and this Ordinance as specified in Annex 1 number 1 applies.
Amended by No I of the O of 11 March 2022, in force since 1 May 2022 (AS 2022 220).

If in this Ordinance reference is made to provisions of the REACH Regulation, the CLP Regulation or Directive 75/324/EEC which in turn refer to other provisions of these acts, these other provisions also apply; the applicable version of the act in question is that specified in the footnote to paragraph 2 letter f or, as applicable, paragraph 4 or, in the case of references to annexes to the CLP Regulation or the REACH Regulation, the version specified in Annex 2 number 1 or, as applicable, Annex 4 number 3. An exception are provisions referred to in provisions of the REACH Regulation and the CLP Regulation, as specified in Annex 1 number 2; here, the provisions of the Swiss legislation listed in Annex 1 number 2 apply instead.
Amended by Annex No 1 of the O of 15 Nov. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 709).

If in this Ordinance reference is made to provisions of the REACH Regulation or the CLP Regulation which in turn refer to other EU legislation, the Swiss legislation specified in Annex 1 number 3 applies instead of the EU legislation.

The provisions of the Nagoya Ordinance of 11 December 2015
SR 451.61 are reserved with respect to the placing on the market of substances and preparations the development of which is based on the use of genetic resources or on traditional knowledge associated therewith.
Inserted by Annex No 2 of the Nagoya Ordinance of 11 Dec. 2015, in force since 1 Feb. 2016 (AS 2016 277).

Substances and preparations are dangerous if they fulfil the criteria for classification of physical, health, environmental or other hazards specified in the technical provisions referred to in Annex 2 number 1.

Substances are considered persistent, bioaccumulative and toxic (PBT) if they fulfil the criteria defined in Sections 1.1.1–1.1.3 of Annex XIII to the REACH Regulation
See footnote to Art. 2 para. 4. .

Substances are considered very persistent and very bioaccumulative (vPvB) if they fulfil the criteria defined in Sections 1.2.1 and 1.2.2 of Annex XIII to the REACH Regulation
See footnote to Art. 2 para. 2 let. f. Name in accordance with Annex No1 of the O of 15 Nov. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024; this amendment has been made in the provisions mentioned in the AS. .

The self-regulation system introduced by Article 5 of the Chemicals Act and Article 26 of the EPA requires manufacturers to assess whether substances or preparations may endanger human life or health or the environment. To this end, manufacturers must classify, package and label substances and preparations and prepare exposure scenarios and compile safety data sheets in accordance with this Ordinance.

In the case of objects containing dangerous substances, substances considered PBT or vPvB, or substances listed in Annex 3, self-regulation under Article 26 of the EPA requires manufacturers to assess whether these substances may endanger the environment or indirectly endanger human health when these objects are used as intended, or in a foreseeable manner, or when they are appropriately disposed of.

In the case of objects containing substances listed in Annex 3, manufacturers must assess whether these substances may endanger human health when these objects are used as intended, or in a foreseeable manner, or when they are appropriately disposed of.
Manufacturers must collect all available data of relevance to the obligations referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2.

Any person importing substances, preparations or objects with dangerous constituents in a professional or commercial capacity must comply with the obligations listed under paragraphs 1 and 2 before supplying them to a third party for the first time or, if they are for the importer’s own use, before using them for the first time.

Manufacturers must classify substances in accordance with Articles 5, 7–13 and 15 of the CLP Regulation
See footnote to Art. 2 para. 4. .

If a harmonised classification is specified for a substance in Annex VI to the CLP Regulation, in the applicable version referred to in Annex 2 number 1, the manufacturer must additionally classify this substance in accordance with Article 4 paragraph 3 of the CLP Regulation.

blockList.listIntroduction: Classification must be based:

item.p: in the case of existing substances: on data collected in accordance with Article 5 paragraph 4;

item.num:
b.
Amended by No I of the O of 31 Jan. 2018, in force since 1 March 2018 (AS 2018 801).
item.p: in the case of new substances: on the data as specified in Article 5 paragraph 4 and on data in the technical dossier as specified in Article 27 paragraph 2 letter b.

content.p: The Federal Department of Home Affairs (FDHA), in consultation with the Federal Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications (DETEC) and the Federal Department of Economic Affairs, Education and Research (EAER), may prescribe a harmonised classification and the associated labelling for certain hazard classes of a substance if, for the substance in question, a harmonised classification is not specified for the relevant hazard class in Annex VI to the CLP Regulation, in the applicable version referred to in Annex 2 number 1.

Manufacturers must classify preparations in accordance with Articles 6–15 of the CLP Regulation
See footnote to Art. 2 para. 4. .

section.heading: Packaging and Labelling of Substances and Preparations

content.p:
Manufacturers making available or supplying dangerous substances or preparations to third parties must package them in accordance with Article 35 of the CLP Regulation
See footnote to Art. 2 para. 4. .

Aerosol dispensers not covered by the FoodA
SR 817.0 are subject both to the packaging provisions of this Ordinance and to Articles 1 and 2, and points 2.1, 2.3, 3, 4, 5 and 6 of the Annex to Directive 75/324/EEC
See footnote to Art. 2 para. 4. .

blockList.listIntroduction: Manufacturers making available or supplying dangerous substances or preparations to third parties must label them in accordance with the following provisions:

item.num:
a.
The correction of 24 April 2023 relates to the French and Italian texts only (AS 2023 193).

item.p: the specific rules for labelling of outer packaging, inner packaging and single packaging set out in Article 33 of the CLP Regulation.

content.p: Preparations with particular hazards referred to in Article 4 paragraph 7 of the CLP Regulation must additionally be labelled in accordance with Article 25 paragraph 6 of the CLP Regulation.

blockList.listIntroduction: In addition to paragraphs 1 and 2, the labelling must meet the following requirements:

item.p: The name, address and telephone number of the manufacturer are to be included.

item.num:
b.
Amended by No I of the O of 11 March 2022, in force since 1 May 2022 (AS 2022 220).
item.p: The labelling must be in an official language of the location at which the substance or preparation is supplied to private or professional users. With the agreement of individual professional users, a substance or a preparation for supply to these users may be labelled in another official language or in English.

Where labelling is in languages other than those required under letter b, all information shall be given in all languages used.
Amended by No I of the O of 31 Jan. 2018, in force since 1 March 2018 (AS 2018 801).

blockList.listIntroduction:
In the case of substances or preparations imported from a member state of the EEA, the manufacturer’s name may be replaced on the labelling by the name of the person responsible for placing on the market in the EEA, if the substances or preparations:
Amended by No I of the O of 11 March 2022, in force since 1 May 2022 (AS 2022 220).

item.p: are not intended for distribution to private users; or

are supplied to private users, are contained in an inner packaging in portions of no more than 125ml or g and are marked on the outer packaging with the name, address and telephone number of the manufacturer.
Inserted by No I of the O of 31 Jan. 2018, in force since 1 March 2018 (AS 2018 801).

content.p: If further label elements are required in order to comply with other legislation, these are to be included in the section for supplemental information in accordance with Article 25 of the CLP Regulation.

Where the name in the IUPAC nomenclature
Chemical nomenclature of the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC): www.iupac.org exceeds 100 characters, another name may be used, provided that the report in accordance with Article 49 includes both the name given in the IUPAC nomenclature and the other name used.

The requirements of paragraph 1 are deemed to have been met if the inner packaging is labelled before the application of or immediately after the removal of the transport packaging. Responsibility for packaging and labelling rests with the manufacturer.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 11 March 2022, in force since 1 May 2022 (AS 2022 220). The correction of 24 April 2023 relates to the French and Italian texts only (AS 2023 193)

content.p: The official languages are German, French and Italian.

Aerosol dispensers not covered by the FoodA
SR 817.0 are subject both to the provisions of this Ordinance and to Articles 1, 2 and 8 paragraphs 1 and 1a, and points 1.8, 1.9 and 1.10, the introductory provision of number 2, and points 2.2 and 2.3 of the Annex to Directive 75/324/EEC
See footnote to Art. 2 para. 4. .
Amended by No I of the O of 31 Jan. 2018, in force since 1 March 2018 (AS 2018 801).

In the case of aerosol dispensers not deemed to be dangerous under Article 3, the manufacturer’s name and address must be indicated. If such an aerosol dispenser is imported from an EEA member state, the manufacturer’s name may be replaced by the name of the person responsible for placing it on the market in the EEA.

blockList.listIntroduction: The Notification Authority may, after consultation with the assessment authorities, permit derogations from the labelling requirements for certain substances or preparations, or for certain groups of substances or preparations, and allow these not to be labelled or to be labelled in some other suitable form if:

item.p: the packages are too small or otherwise unsuitable for labelling in accordance with Article 10;
the substance or preparation is supplied in such small quantities that, taking the particular hazards into account, it poses no risk to humans or the environment; or

the substance or preparation does not fall within the scope of the CLP Regulation
See footnote to Art. 2 para. 4. .

content.p: It shall issue a ruling in response to a justified application or issue a general ruling.
It shall maintain a list of the derogations that have been permitted and publish this on its website.

authorialNote.p: Repealed by No III 1 of the O of 22 March 2017, with effect from 1 May 2017 (AS 2017 2593).

article.heading: Use of an alternative chemical name

blockList.listIntroduction: Manufacturers of preparations may use an alternative chemical name for a substance if:

item.p: they demonstrate that disclosing the name of the substance on the label or in the safety data sheet would put the confidential nature of their business, in particular their intellectual property rights, at risk; and
the substance meets the criteria specified in Section 1.4 of Annex I to the CLP Regulation, in the applicable version referred to in Annex 2 number 1.

content.p: The alternative chemical name shall be a name that identifies the most important functional groups or serves as an alternative designation.

blockList.listIntroduction: If the European Chemicals Agency has approved the use of an alternative chemical name in accordance with Article 24 of the CLP Regulation, the use of the name is deemed approved in Switzerland from the date on which the Notification Authority acknowledges the following documents and data:

item.p: the decision of the European Chemicals Agency;

details of the substance identity in accordance with Article 49 letter c numbers 1–3.
Amended by Annex No 1 of the O of 15 Nov. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 709).

content.p:
Where the name and identification number in the classification and labelling inventory in accordance with Article 42 of the CLP Regulation is used when the chemical name in accordance with Article 18 paragraph 2 letter b of the CLP Regulation is used, if the Notification Authority so requests, the substance identity in accordance with Annex VI Sections 2.1–2.3 of the REACH Regulation
See footnote to Art. 2 para. 2 let. f. must be provided.
Inserted by Annex No 1 of the O of 15 Nov. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 709).

blockList.listIntroduction: The use of an alternative chemical name may be requested for a preparation:

item.p: in a specific composition;
with a specific trade name or a specific designation; and
reserved for certain uses.

content.p: Authorisation to use an alternative chemical name is granted to the manufacturer and is non-transferable.

blockList.listIntroduction: The use of an alternative chemical name by the manufacturer and professional users in the same supply chain is permitted without authorisation for the first six years after:

item.p: the reporting, declaration or notification of a new substance;

the registration of a substance that falls under Article 119 paragraph 2 letter f of the REACH Regulation and in respect of which proof of registration and details of the substance identity in accordance with Article 49 letter c numbers 1–3 are submitted to the Notification Authority.
Amended by Annex No 1 of the O of 15 Nov. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 709).

content.p:
If no request to use an alternative chemical name and no decision from the European Chemicals Agency nor the information in accordance with paragraph 3 are submitted within the period specified in paragraph 6, on expiry of the period the chemical name in accordance with Article 18 paragraph 2 of the CLP Regulation must be used.
Inserted by Annex No 1 of the O of 15 Nov. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 709).

article.heading: Requests to use an alternative chemical name

content.p: Requests to use an alternative chemical name for a substance in a preparation must be written in an official language or in English and be submitted electronically in the format required by the Notification Authority. The accompanying letter must be written in an official language.

blockList.listIntroduction: Requests must contain:

item.p: the manufacturer’s name, address and telephone number;

blockList.listIntroduction: the following information relating to the substances whose identity is to remain confidential on the label:

item.p: the chemical name,

the Chemical Abstracts Service (CAS) registry number
The CAS registry number can be accessed free of charge on the European Chemicals Agency website: http://echa.europa.eu/information-on-chemicals/ec-inventory ,
the EC number;
the alternative name of the substance;
the reasons for the request;
the trade name or designation of the preparation;
the information on the constituents in accordance with the provisions relating to the safety data sheet;
the classification of the preparation;
the labelling of the preparation;
the intended uses of the preparation;
the physical state;
if applicable, the safety data sheet.

content.p: The Notification Authority shall decide on the request in consultation with the assessment authorities.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 31 Jan. 2018 (AS 2018 801). Amended by Annex No 1 of the O of 18 Nov. 2020, in force since 1 Jan. 2022 (AS 2020 5125).

content.p: If a manufacturer places a preparation on the market which is classified as dangerous because of the physical or health hazards it poses, the manufacturer must label the preparation with a unique formula identifier (UFI).

He must generate the UFI using the electronic system provided by the Notification Authority. Generating the UFI using the electronic system is not required if the preparation already has a UFI that has been generated on the basis of the CLP Regulation
See footnote to Art. 2 para. 4. .

blockList.listIntroduction: The UFI, preceded by the acronym "UFI:" in capital letters, must be printed or affixed in a clearly visible, legible and indelible manner in the following location:

item.p: on the label in the section for supplemental information in accordance with Article 2525 of the CLP Regulation; or

on the inner packaging together with the other label elements; if the inner packaging is of such a nature or so small that the UFI cannot be printed or affixed thereon, it may be printed or affixed with the other label elements on the outer packaging.

content.p: In the case of preparation that are not packaged, the UFI must be indicated on the safety data sheet or, in the case of supply to private users, in a copy of the label elements in accordance with Article 29 paragraph 3 of the CLP Regulation, together with the other label elements.
Paragraphs 1–4 do not apply if the preparation is not subject to the obligation to notify in accordance with Article 54.

section.heading: Exposure Scenarios and Safety Data Sheet for Substances and Preparations

content.p:
The manufacturer of an existing substance that fulfils the criteria specified in Article 14 paragraph 4 of the REACH Regulation
See footnote to Art. 2 para. 4. and is supplied on its own to third parties in a total quantity of 10 tonnes per year or more must prepare an exposure scenario for each identified use of the substance.

Any person who obtains a substance for which exposure scenarios have been prepared and supplies it to third parties on a commercial basis in quantities of 1 tonne per year or more as a substance or in a preparation for a use not described in the safety data sheet must prepare an exposure scenario for this use.

blockList.listIntroduction: Paragraph 2 does not apply in cases where:

item.p: the exposure scenario for the new use would exclusively cover conditions described in an exposure scenario included in the safety data sheet;
the substance is present in the preparation in a concentration below the limits referred to in Article 27 paragraph 3; or
the substance is used for purposes of product and process-orientated research and development.

article.heading: Requirements for the preparation of exposure scenarios

content.p:
The exposure scenarios must be prepared in accordance with the provisions of Section 5.1 of Annex I to the REACH Regulation
See footnote to Art. 2 para. 4. .

article.heading: Purpose of the safety data sheet

content.p: Safety data sheets are designed to enable professional users or traders to take the measures required for health protection, occupational safety and environmental protection.

article.heading: Obligation to compile a safety data sheet

blockList.listIntroduction: Where the provision of a safety data sheet is required under Article 21, the manufacturer must compile a safety data sheet for the following substances and preparations:

item.p: dangerous substances and preparations;
PBT or vPvB substances;
substances listed in Annex 3;

blockList.listIntroduction: preparations which are not dangerous within the meaning of Article 3 and contain at least one of the following substances:

item.p: a substance that is dangerous to health or to the environment in an individual concentration of ≥1.0 per cent by weight (non-gaseous preparations) or ≥0.2 per cent by volume (gaseous preparations),

item.num:
2.
Amended by No I of the O of 31 Jan. 2018, in force since 1 March 2018 (AS 2018 801).
item.p: a category 2 carcinogenic substance, a category 1A, 1B or 2 toxic for reproduction substance, a category 1 skin allergen, a category 1 inhalation allergen, a substance having effects on or through lactation, or a PBT or vPvB substance in an individual concentration of ≥0.1 per cent by weight,
a substance listed in Annex 3 in an individual concentration of ≥0.1 per cent by weight,

item.num:
4.
Amended by Annex No 1 of the O of 18 Nov. 2020, in force since 15 Dec. 2020 (AS 2020 5125).
item.p:
a substance for which an occupational exposure limit value has been laid down in Directives 2000/39/EC

article.heading: Requirements for the compilation of safety data sheets

content.p: Safety data sheets must be compiled in accordance with the technical provisions referred to in Annex 2 Number 3.

The exposure scenarios prepared in accordance with Article 16 or included in the chemical safety report (Art. 28) must be attached to the safety data sheet; the information in sections 1, 7, 8 and 13 of the safety data sheet must correspond to the uses described in the exposure scenarios.
The FDHA may, in consultation with DETEC and the EAER, define the technical expertise required for the compilation of safety data sheets.

article.heading: Obligation to provide safety data sheets

content.p: Anyone who supplies substances or preparations as specified in Article 19 to professional users or traders in a commercial capacity must provide them with a current safety data sheet. In retail outlets, the safety data sheet must be provided on request.

blockList.listIntroduction: The safety data sheet must be provided:

item.p: when supplying a substance or preparation as specified in Article 19 letters a–c: at the latest at the time it is first supplied and on request with subsequent deliveries;
when supplying a preparation as specified in Article 19 letter d: on request.

blockList.listIntroduction: Safety data sheets must be provided as follows:

item.p: free of charge;
in the official languages requested by the professional user or trader or, by mutual agreement, in another language; the annex to the safety data sheet may be written in English;
on paper or in electronic form; the safety data sheet is to be provided on paper if this is requested by the professional user or trader.

content.p: If important new information on a substance or preparation becomes available, the manufacturer must update the safety data sheet without delay.
The supplier must make the updated safety data sheet available to all professional users or traders supplied with the substance or preparation concerned within the previous twelve months.
Paragraph 2 does not apply to safety data sheets provided through retail outlets.

article.heading: Obligation to retain safety data sheets

content.p: Professional users or traders are required to retain the safety data sheet for as long as the substance or preparation concerned continues to be handled at their workplace.

chapter.heading: Notification and Declaration of New Substances

blockList.listIntroduction: Manufacturers of a new substance or their exclusive representative must notify the new substance to the Notification Authority before placing it on the market for the first time:

item.p: on its own;
in a preparation; or
in an object from which the new substance may be released under normal or reasonably foreseeable conditions of use.

content.p: If a new substance is contained in a polymer as a monomer or as another substance in the form of monomer units or chemically bound, paragraph 1 applies for the substance on its own.
The Notification Authority may require the notification of a substance contained in an object if it has reason to believe that the substance may be released when the object is used.

section.heading: Use of Data from Previous Notifiers and Data Protection Period

article.heading: Use of data from previous notifiers

content.p:
If the Notification Authority finds that a new substance has already been notified in Switzerland, it shall inform the notifier of the names and addresses of the earlier notifiers.
Inserted by No I of the O of 31 Jan. 2018, in force since 1 March 2018 (AS 2018 801).

blockList.listIntroduction: The Notification Authority may refer to data from a previous notifier instead of data produced by the notifier if:

item.p: the new notifier proves with a letter of access from a previous notifier that the latter agrees to the Notification Authority consulting its data; or

the data protection period has expired.

blockList.listIntroduction: The notifier must not refer to data from previous notifiers regarding:

item.p: the identity and purity of the substance and the nature of any impurities;
action to render the substance harmless.

content.p: The rules of competition and intellectual property law are not affected by the provisions of this section.

The data protection period is 12 years.
Amended by No I of the O of 11 March 2022, in force since 1 May 2022 (AS 2022 220).

For additional data which must be submitted in accordance with Article 47, the protection period is 5 years. If the data protection period specified in paragraph 1 has not yet expired, the protection period for additional data is extended accordingly.

article.heading: Mandatory advance enquiries to avoid tests on vertebrates

content.p:
Anyone planning tests on vertebrates for notification purposes must contact the Notification Authority to enquire whether data from such tests is already available. The enquiry must be made in the format stipulated by the Notification Authority.
Amended by No I of the O of 11 March 2022, in force since 1 May 2022 (AS 2022 220).

blockList.listIntroduction: This enquiry must contain information on:

item.p: the identity of the substance in accordance with Article 27 paragraph 2 letter b number 2;
the quantity of substance the applicant intends to place on the market.

blockList.listIntroduction: If the Notification Authority already has adequate data from previous tests on vertebrates, and none of the conditions of Article 29 paragraph 1bis is met, then:

item.p: it shall notify the former notifiers of the intended use of the data by the new notifier and of his name and address, and
it shall disclose the names and addresses of the former notifiers to the new notifier.

content.p: Studies on tests with vertebrates may not be repeated.

article.heading: Right to remuneration for sharing of data from previous tests on vertebrates

content.p: The previous notifiers are entitled to receive fair remuneration from the new notifier for the use of their data from previous tests on vertebrates if the term of protection for such data has not yet expired.
The notifiers shall take steps independently to reach an agreement on data sharing and remuneration. They may seek an arbitrator’s report.

If no agreement is reached, the new notifier may apply to the Notification Authority for a ruling on the amount of the remuneration; the request may be made no earlier than four months after receipt of the notification referred to in Article 31 paragraph 3. The new notifier shall inform the previous notifiers of his/her application.

blockList.listIntroduction:
The Notification Authority shall issue a ruling on the amount of the remuneration no later than 60 days after the request referred to in paragraph 3. If an arbitrator’s report has been submitted, the Notification Authority is bound by it unless the parties raise objections within 30 days in terms of Article 189 paragraph 3 of the Civil Procedure Code
SR 272 . In the absence of an arbitrator’s report, the Notification Authority shall take particular account in its ruling of:

item.p: the costs incurred by the previous notifiers in obtaining the test results;
the remaining period of protection for the data concerned.

article.heading: Use of data from previous tests on vertebrates

blockList.listIntroduction: The Notification Authority shall use data from previous tests on vertebrates for notification under Article 24, unless otherwise agreed between notifiers, as soon as:

item.p: the new notifier and the previous notifiers have concluded an agreement on the sharing of data and the remuneration, or the Notification Authority has issued a corresponding ruling, and
the new notifier pays the remuneration or has undertaken to do so by acknowledgement of debt confirmed by signature.

section.heading: Declaration of New Substances for Product and Process-orientated Research and Development

content.p: If the substance quantity placed on the market is 1 tonne per year or more and if the new substance is exempt from notification under Article 26 paragraph 1 letter d, the manufacturer or his exclusive representative must declare the new substance to the Notification Authority before placing it on the market for the first time either on its own or as a constituent in a preparation or object from which the substance is intended to be released under normal or reasonably foreseeable conditions of use.

article.heading: Form and content of the declaration

content.p: The declaration must be written in an official language or in English and be submitted electronically in the format required by the Notification Authority. The accompanying letter must be written in an official language.

blockList.listIntroduction: The declaration must contain the following information and documents:

item.p: the name and address of the manufacturer;
if the manufacturer has imported the substance: the name and address of the foreign manufacturer;
essential data relating to the identity of the substance;
the intended uses;
the amount of the substance that the manufacturer expects to place on the market each year in Switzerland;
proposed classification and labelling;
the research programme and a list of the people to whom the substance is to be supplied;
in the case of dangerous substances or PBT or vPvB substances: a proposed safety data sheet.

content.p: The Notification Authority may request the manufacturer or exclusive representative to furnish test reports that are relevant for the assessment of the substance, provided that they are available and can be obtained with reasonable effort.

article.heading: Confirmation of receipt and forwarding of the documents

content.p: The Notification Authority shall confirm to the manufacturer or the exclusive representative the date on which the notification or declaration was received.
If the documents are not obviously incomplete, the Notification Authority shall forward them to the assessment authorities.

article.heading: Review of the notification or declaration

blockList.listIntroduction: The assessment authorities, within their area of competence, shall assess whether:

item.p: the submission is complete or if not, whether the reasons given by the notifier are valid;
the data is scientifically plausible;
the test reports are based on tests meeting the requirements specified in Article 43.

content.p: If, when reviewing the notification dossier, an assessment authority determines that a substance poses a particular risk for human health or the environment, on account of its dangerous nature, its properties, its foreseeable use or the quantity placed on the market, the authority may conduct a targeted risk assessment before accepting the notification.
The assessment authorities shall report the results of their review to the Notification Authority.
If the Notification Authority determines that the documents are obviously incomplete, it shall inform the manufacturer or exclusive representative accordingly without delay.

If an assessment authority determines that the documents are incomplete or inaccurate, or that further data or tests are required for an assessment of the hazards and risks associated with the substance, it shall inform the Notification Authority accordingly. The Notification Authority shall request the manufacturer or exclusive representative to submit additions or corrections.

If a robust study summary in accordance with Article 27 paragraph 2 letter b numbers 7–9 does not permit an independent assessment of a specific test, the Notification Authority may request the full study report.
The Notification Authority shall confirm to the manufacturer or exclusive representative the date of receipt of additions and corrections.

article.heading: Acceptance of the notification or declaration

content.p: In consultation with the assessment authorities, the Notification Authority shall issue a ruling on the acceptance of the notification or declaration if the review has shown that the notification or declaration documents are complete and sufficient to permit assessment of the hazards and risks associated with the substance.
If a targeted risk assessment was conducted, the ruling shall include the risk mitigation measures ordered.

section.heading: Authorisation to Place Substances on the Market

article.heading: Placing substances subject to notification requirements on the market

blockList.listIntroduction: Substances subject to notification requirements may be placed on the market if:

item.p: the Notification Authority has accepted the notification thereof; or
60 days have elapsed since the confirmed date of receipt of the notification and of any additions or corrections required thereafter, without the Notification Authority having issued any response.

article.heading: Placing substances subject to declaration requirements on the market

blockList.listIntroduction: Substances subject to declaration requirements may be placed on the market if:

item.p: the Notification Authority has accepted the declaration thereof; or
30 days have elapsed since the confirmed date of receipt of the declaration and of any additions or corrections required thereafter, without the Notification Authority having issued any response.

content.p: Manufacturers must ensure that the conduct of the tests required for assessment of the hazards and risks of substances and preparations, the methods used and the assessment of test results are in accordance with the current state of scientific and technical knowledge.

They must not carry out tests on vertebrates if the hazards can be assessed by other methods or if the test is not necessary from a scientific point of view.
Inserted by No I of the O of 31 Jan. 2018, in force since 1 March 2018 (AS 2018 801).
The FDHA, DETEC and the EAER may regulate technical details in their respective areas of competence.

Tests designed to determine the properties of substances and preparations must be carried out in accordance with the test methods specified in the technical provisions referred to in Annex 2 number 2.

blockList.listIntroduction: Other test methods may be used if:

item.p: no method is specified in accordance with paragraph 1;
the manufacturer can show that a specified method is not suitable for the determination of a given physicochemical property; or

the method is recognised in the EU in accordance with Article 13 paragraph 3 of the REACH Regulation
See footnote to Art. 2 para. 4. .

blockList.listIntroduction: If other test methods are used, the manufacturer must show that they:

item.p: produce valid results; and
take due account of animal protection in the case of tests on animals.

content.p:
Non-clinical tests designed to determine properties dangerous to health or the environment must be carried out in accordance with the principles of Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) specified in the Ordinance of 18 May 2005
SR 813.112.1 on Good Laboratory Practice.

If certain tests do not, or do not fully, comply with GLP principles, the person submitting the test reports must state the reasons. The Notification Authority, in consultation with the assessment authorities, shall decide whether to accept these test results.

article.heading: Reassessment of substances, preparations and objects

blockList.listIntroduction: Manufacturers must reassess or further assess substances, preparations and objects containing dangerous constituents and, where necessary, reclassify, relabel and repackage them if:

item.p: they are to be supplied for different purposes;
they are to be used in a different way;
they are to be used in much larger quantities than before;
variations arise in the nature and quantity of impurities, which could have adverse effects on human health or the environment;
the assessment of the risks they pose to human health or the environment needs to be modified in the light of practical experience, new data or new information.

content.p: Manufacturers are required to update documents continuously with new information relevant to health and the environment for as long as they continue to place on the market the substance, preparation or object containing dangerous constituents.

They must retain or ensure the availability of the main documents used in the assessment and classification, together with the results of the assessment and classification, for at least ten years after the products are last placed on the market. They must retain samples and specimens for as long as their condition allows them to be analysed.

title.heading: Rules for Handling of Substances, Preparations and Objects

article.heading: Taking account of the information provided by the manufacturer

content.p: Substances, preparations and objects may be promoted, offered or supplied professionally or commercially only for the uses and methods of disposal stated by the manufacturer.
The information and instructions given on the package and labelling and in the safety data sheet must be taken into account.
Substances and preparations may be released directly into the environment only to the extent that is necessary for the intended use.

blockList.listIntroduction: To this end, users must:

item.p: use equipment allowing correct and accurate application;
take measures to prevent substances and preparations, as far as possible, from entering surrounding areas or waterbodies; and
take measures to ensure that, as far as possible, animals, plants, their biological communities and habitats are not threatened.

content.p: Preparations may be released directly into the environment only for the uses specified by the manufacturer.
When substances and preparations are stored, the information and instructions given on the package and labelling and, if applicable, in the safety data sheet must be taken into account.
Dangerous substances and preparations and their containers must be protected against hazardous, especially mechanical, impacts.

Dangerous substances and preparations must be clearly identifiable and kept separate from other goods. No foodstuffs, animal feedingstuffs or therapeutic products may be kept in the immediate vicinity.
Paragraphs 1–3 also apply to objects from which substances or preparations are released in quantities that may endanger human health or the environment.
Substances and preparations that may react dangerously with each other must be stored separately.

blockList.listIntroduction: Dangerous substances and preparations may only be filled into and stored in containers which meet the following requirements:

item.p: They must not be capable of being confused with packaging containing foodstuffs, cosmetics, therapeutic products or animal feedingstuffs.
The name of the substance or preparation must be given in the labelling of the containers.

They must comply with the requirements of Article 35 paragraphs 1 and 3 of the CLP Regulation
See footnote to Art. 2 para. 4. .
Their design must not be likely to attract or arouse the curiosity of children.

article.heading: Special obligations with regard to the supply of substances and preparations

content.p: Anyone who supplies a substance or preparation in a commercial capacity and is required to provide a safety data sheet must be familiar with and capable of interpreting the content of the safety data sheet.
Commercial and educational establishments must notify the cantonal enforcement authorities of their chemicals contact person, designated under Article 25 paragraph 2 of the Chemicals Act.
The FDHA shall regulate mandatory notification in accordance with paragraph 1; it shall define the form and content of the notification.
It shall define the requirements that the chemicals contact person must meet, particularly with regard to technical qualifications and operational responsibilities.

Advertising for substances, preparations and objects must not give a misleading impression as to the risks posed to human health and the environment or as to their environmental acceptability, and must not encourage inappropriate or illegitimate use or disposal.

Terms such as «degradable», «not harmful to the environment», «non-polluting» and «non-water-polluting» may be used in advertising only if the properties thus described are at the same time explained in more detail.

Anyone who advertises dangerous substances or preparations that private users can purchase without seeing the labelling beforehand must indicate their hazardous properties in a comprehensible and clearly legible or audible manner.

Paragraph 3 also applies to preparations labelled in accordance with Article 25 paragraph 6 of the CLP Regulation
See footnote to Art. 2 para. 4. .
Substances and preparations must not be promoted for uses for which they are not to be placed on the market.

chapter.heading: Handling Substances and Preparations in Groups 1 and 2

article.heading: Substances and preparations in Groups 1 and 2

blockList.listIntroduction: Substances and preparations are deemed to belong to Group 1:

item.p:
if their labelling in accordance with the CLP Regulation
See footnote to Art. 2 para. 4. contains at least one element specified in number 1.1 of Annex 5 to this Ordinance; or
if they are not yet labelled in accordance with the CLP Regulation and their labelling contains at least one element specified in number 2.1 of Annex 5 to this Ordinance.

blockList.listIntroduction: Substances and preparations are deemed to belong to Group 2:

item.p: if their labelling in accordance with the CLP Regulation contains at least one element specified in number 1.2 of Annex 5 to this Ordinance; or
if they are not yet labelled in accordance with the CLP Regulation and their labelling contains at least one element specified in number 2.2 of Annex 5 to this Ordinance.

content.p: For the storage of substances or preparations in Groups 1 and 2, Article 57 applies.
Anyone who stores substances or preparations in Groups 1 and 2 must ensure that they are not accessible to unauthorised persons.
Substances and preparations in Groups 1 and 2 may only be filled into and stored in containers if these are labelled with the appropriate danger symbols or hazard pictograms.
Substances and preparations in Group 2 which are intended for private users must not be offered on a self-service basis.
The prohibition specified in paragraph 1 does not apply to motor fuels.
Substances and preparations in Group 1 must not be commercially supplied to private users.
Substances and preparations in Groups 1 and 2 may be commercially supplied only to persons having capacity to act.

Substances and preparations in Groups 1 and 2 may be supplied to minors if they are capable of judgement and have to handle these substances or preparations in the course of their training or in a professional or commercial capacity.
The supply restrictions specified in paragraphs 1 and 2 do not apply to motor fuels.

article.heading: Special obligations with regard to supply

content.p: Anyone who commercially supplies a substance or preparation in Group 1 to professional users or traders must, at the time of supply, explicitly inform them of the precautions required and the correct method of disposal.

Anyone who commercially supplies a substance or preparation in Group 2 to private users must, at the time of supply, explicitly inform them of the precautions required and the correct method of disposal.

Substances and preparations may be supplied in accordance with paragraph 2 only to persons who can be assumed by the supplier to be capable of judgement and able to comply with the duty of care specified in Article 8 of the Chemicals Act and the requirements set out in Article 28 of the EPA.
The obligations specified in paragraphs 1 and 2 do not apply to the supply of motor fuels.

blockList.listIntroduction: Special knowledge is required by anyone who, in a commercial capacity:

item.p: supplies substances and preparations in Group 1 to persons who obtain them in order to use them professionally, but without placing them on the market in a different form;
supplies substances and preparations in Group 2 to private users.

blockList.listIntroduction: The FDHA may regulate:

item.p: how the knowledge requirements are to be met; in this connection, it shall take professional training and experience into account;
the content, duration and organisation of courses for people seeking to acquire such knowledge.

content.p:
Articles 10 and 11 of the Chemical Risk Reduction Ordinance of 18 May 2005
SR 814.81 (ORRChem) apply mutatis mutandis.
Paragraph 1 does not apply to motor fuels.

article.heading: Theft, loss, erroneous placing on the market

content.p: In the event of theft or loss of substances or preparations in Group 1, the person suffering the theft or loss must notify the police without delay.
The police must inform the cantonal authority responsible for enforcing this Ordinance as well as the Federal Office of Police.

blockList.listIntroduction: Anyone who erroneously places on the market a substance or a preparation in Group 1 or 2 must immediately inform the cantonal authority responsible for enforcing this Ordinance and provide the following information:

item.p: all the data required for precise identification of the substance or preparation;
a comprehensive description of the danger which the substance or preparation may pose;
all the available information as to the source from which the substance or preparation was obtained and to whom the substance or preparation has been supplied;
the measures taken to avert any danger, such as warnings, suspension of sales, withdrawal from the market or recall.

content.p: The cantonal authority shall decide whether and in what way the public needs to be warned of any danger.
Substances and preparations in Groups 1 and 2 may be provided for promotional purposes only to professional users or traders.

article.heading: Substances and preparations intended for self-defence

content.p: For the handling of substances and preparations intended for self-defence, Article 62, Article 64 paragraphs 2 and 3, Article 65 paragraphs 2 and 3, Article 66 paragraph 1 letter b, Article 67 paragraphs 3 and 4 and Article 68 apply mutatis mutandis.
Substances and preparations intended for self-defence must not be offered on a self-service basis.

level.heading: General notifier information

blockList.listIntroduction: 2.1 The identity of the notifier is to be indicated, in particular:

item.p: Name, address, telephone number and e-mail address;
Contact person;
Location of the notifier’s production site(s), as appropriate.

blockList.listIntroduction: 2.2 If the notifier is an exclusive representative, the following information is to be additionally provided:

item.p: Name and address of the foreign manufacturer;
Location of the production site(s);
Authorisation from the foreign manufacturer stating that it has designated the notifier as its exclusive representative;
Names and addresses of the importers represented;
the substance quantities that each importer expects to import annually.

level.heading: Identification of the substance

blockList.listIntroduction: The following information on the substance is to be provided:

item.p: data specified in Section 2 of Annex VI to the REACH Regulation;
for nanomaterials: data on composition and, where available, surface coating and surface functionalisation.

level.heading: Information on manufacture and use

blockList.listIntroduction: The following information is to be provided:

item.p: the estimated overall quantity to be placed on the market by the notifier in the calendar year of the notification;
the quantities for the notifier’s own use;
the form or physical state in which the substance is made available;
a brief description of the identified use(s);
information on waste quantities and composition of waste resulting from manufacture of the substance, the use in objects and identified uses;
uses advised against (Section 1.2 of the safety data sheet).

level.heading: Classification and Labelling

blockList.listIntroduction: The following is to be indicated:

item.p: the labelling of the substance in accordance with Article 10;
any specific concentration limits resulting from the application of Article 10 of the CLP Regulation.

level.heading: Guidance on safe use

blockList.listIntroduction: The following information is to be provided; it must be consistent with that in the safety data sheet, where such a safety data sheet is required in accordance with Article 19:

item.p: first-aid measures (safety data sheet, No 4);
fire-fighting measures (safety data sheet, No 5);
accidental release measures (safety data sheet, No 6);
handling and storage (safety data sheet, No 7);
transport information (safety data sheet, No 14);
exposure controls/personal protection (safety data sheet, No 8);
stability and reactivity (safety data sheet, No 10);
disposal considerations: information on recycling and methods of disposal for industry and for the public (safety data sheet, No 13).

level.heading: Information on exposure (1–10 tonnes per year)

blockList.listIntroduction: For substances where the quantity placed on the market is between 1 and 10 tonnes per year, the following information on exposure is to be provided:
Main use categories:

item.p: professional use,
industrial use,
private use;

blockList.listIntroduction: Specification for industrial and professional use:

item.p: use in a closed system,
use resulting in inclusion into or onto matrix,
non-dispersive use by a restricted number of persons,
dispersive use;

blockList.listIntroduction: Significant routes of exposure:

item.p: human exposure: oral, dermal and inhalatory,
environmental exposure: water, air, solid waste and soil,
pattern of exposure: accidental/infrequent, occasional or continuous/ frequent.

level.heading: Information on physicochemical properties

blockList.listIntroduction: The following information is to be provided:
for the quantities placed on the market of 1 tonne per year or more:

item.p: robust study summaries with regard to the information specified in Section 7 of Annex VII to the REACH Regulation,
for nanomaterials: the particle form and mean particle size and, where available, the number size distribution, specific surface area by volume and aggregation status;

for the quantities placed on the market of 100 tonnes per year or more: in addition to the information specified in letter a, robust study summaries with regard to the information specified in Section 7 of Annex IX to the REACH Regulation.

level.heading: Toxicological information
